entry.title: 2026 Rachmiel Levine–Arthur Riggs Diabetes Research Symposium

link.title: 2026 Rachmiel Levine–Arthur Riggs Diabetes Research Symposium

entry.content: The 2026 Rachmiel Levine–Arthur Riggs Diabetes Research Symposium, organized by City of Hope, took place at The Westin Pasadena in Pasadena, California, USA, from October 16 to 19, 2026. The symposium brought together researchers and clinicians to discuss advances in diabetes research and emerging therapeutic strategies. The scientific program featured twelve thematic sessions covering cell therapy management, economics, and the regulatory landscape of cell replacement for type 1 diabetes; gene-edited stem cells and emerging approaches to cell protection; technologies, omics, and metabolic imaging for targeted drug delivery in vivo; circadian rhythms in stem cell programming and islet function; next-generation immunotherapies; CAR regulatory T cells and β-cell-targeting regulatory T cells; interactions between immune cells and β cells; intra- and extra-islet communication; β-cell regenerative therapies; β-cell mass imaging; transcriptomics in type 1 diabetes; and spatial and metabolic imaging in type 1 diabetes. Dr. Huixia Ren and Dr. Chunmei Zhou attended the symposium and presented their research on pancreatic islet function and glucose homeostasis. During the session on intra- and extra-islet communication, Dr. Ren delivered an oral presentation entitled “Global Synchronization of Pancreatic Islets Maintains Fasting Glycemia In Vivo,” which generated considerable interest among diabetes researchers in attendance. Dr. Zhou presented a poster entitled “Paracrine Temporal Dynamics Shape First-phase Insulin Secretion within Pancreatic Islets” and was honored with the 2026 Levine–Riggs Symposium Scientific Achievement Award. Following the symposium, Dr. Ren and Dr. Zhou visited City of Hope, the symposium’s host institution.

entry.title: SCSC 2026 Award for Real-Time Insulin Secretion Monitoring Research

link.title: SCSC 2026 Award for Real-Time Insulin Secretion Monitoring Research

entry.content: The 2026 International Symposium on Calcium Signaling and Cell Function, also known as the 14th Symposium on Calcium Signaling in China (SCSC 2026), was successfully held in Jinan, Shandong Province, from October 11 to 15, 2026. The symposium brought together leading experts and scholars from around the world to deliver invited talks and engage in in-depth discussions across six frontier themes: (1) Calcium signaling and related ion channels; (2) Calcium stores and calcium-binding proteins; (3) GPCRs in cell function; (4) Calcium signaling in health and disease; (5) Drug targets and new drug research and development; and (6) Advanced technologies of calcium signal detection. Dr. Wenlong Huang participated in the symposium and presented his latest research on real-time insulin secretion monitoring. His poster, entitled “Quantitative, Real-Time Insulin Secretion Monitoring and Ca²⁺ Correlation Revealed by an Extracellular ATP Sensor,” was well received by attendees. In recognition of this work, Dr. Huang was honored with the SCSC 2026 Memorial Award.

entry.title: 2026 Capital International Medical Innovation Forum
entry.content: September 19–20 – The Capital International Medical Innovation Forum and the 2026 Annual Academic Conference of the Capital Medical Sciences Innovation Center were held in Beijing, China, from September 19 to 20, 2026. Bringing together approximately 650 experts and scholars from renowned research institutions, universities, and hospitals worldwide, alongside researchers and graduate students from the Innovation Center, the two-day conference provided a dynamic platform for academic exchange and scientific discussion. Participants explored cutting-edge advances across a wide range of biomedical fields, including regenerative medicine, cancer research, molecular and cellular therapies, immunology, medical physiology, and biomedical artificial intelligence. The conference featured six thematic forums comprising 41 high-level academic presentations, addressing key frontiers in medical science and innovation. Topics included regenerative medicine, cancer research and the development of novel therapeutic strategies, immunology, target identification and validation for therapeutic drug development, medical physiology, and biomedical artificial intelligence, highlighting emerging opportunities and challenges in biomedical research and clinical translation. During the conference, Dr. Huixia Ren delivered an academic presentation entitled Global Synchronization of Pancreatic Islets Maintains Fasting Glycemia In Vivo, exploring the role of coordinated pancreatic islet activity in maintaining fasting blood glucose homeostasis in vivo. In addition to the academic presentation, every member of Ren Lab presented a research poster and actively engaged in scientific discussions and exchanges with fellow researchers at the Innovation Center, sharing research findings and fostering potential collaborations. Beyond the scientific program, Ren Lab also demonstrated its strong team spirit during the conference’s fun tug-of-war competition. Joining forces with Zhang Wei Lab, the team achieved an impressive second-place finish, celebrating both teamwork and camaraderie within the research community.

entry.title: Jonathan S. Marvin’s Lecture on Sensors for Tracking Neurotransmitter Release in Living Animals

link.title: Jonathan S. Marvin’s Lecture on Sensors for Tracking Neurotransmitter Release in Living Animals

entry.content: September 15th – Jonathan S. Marvin, Senior Scientist at the Janelia Research Campus, HHMI, gave a seminar entitled “Sensors for Tracking Neurotransmitter Release in Living Animals” at the CIMR Innovation Hub, North Basic Research Building. He introduced the development and application of genetically encoded fluorescent biosensors for monitoring neurotransmitters, neuromodulators, and metabolites with high spatial and temporal resolution in living systems. In particular, he highlighted recent work on iGlucoSnFR2, a second-generation fluorescent glucose sensor capable of measuring intracellular and extracellular glucose dynamics in vivo. He further discussed how membrane-localized iGlucoSnFR2 can be calibrated to quantify changes in extracellular glucose concentration, providing a powerful approach for investigating glucose dynamics at cellular resolution in living animals.

entry.title: 2026 Chinese Biophysics Congress
entry.content: July 30th – The 2026 Chinese Biophysics Congress took place at the Boao Forum for Asia Convention Centre in Hainan, China, from July 30 to August 3, 2026. Serving as China’s largest‑scale and most prestigious academic event for biophysical research, the congress addresses recent breakthroughs and emerging trends within biophysics and its associated disciplines. Centered upon the theme “Biophysics and Human Health”, the conference includes twenty‑nine sub‑themes covering frontier multi‑omics technologies for human‑health research, cutting‑edge‑enabled scientific discovery, novel advances and applications of cryo‑electron microscopy, calcium‑signal decoding: from atomic‑resolution structures to physiological networks, tumor immunity and early‑stage disease prevention, AI‑assisted biology, metabolic pathways governing obesity‑driven tumor progression, translational‑medicine advances for the diagnosis and management of rare metabolic disorders, and nanobiotechnology‑powered precision diagnostics, therapeutics and regenerative‑medicine research. During the conference, PhD candidates Yawen Deng, Xuejiao Wang and Sen Yang presented posters entitled In Vivo Islet Ca²⁺ Dynamics as a Functional Readout of α–β Cell Interaction in Glucose Homeostasis, Glucose Regulation and Obesity‑Mediated Alterations in Endogenous Somatostatin Secretion from Pancreatic δ‑Cells and α‑δ Paracrine Signaling Regulates β‑Cell Activation and Inactivation Thresholds to Enable Directional Glucose Sensing in Pancreatic Islets, respectively.

entry.title: Prof. Sergei Maslov’s Lecture on Protein Language Models

link.title: Prof. Sergei Maslov’s Lecture on Protein Language Models

entry.content: July 29 – Professor Sergei Maslov from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign gave a seminar entitled “From Protein Sequence to Biological Function: What Protein Language Models Know.” He introduced how protein language models extract meaningful representations from large-scale amino acid sequence datasets and outlined advances from protein-family classification to the analysis of intrinsically disordered regions. Drawing on recent studies, Professor Maslov further discussed how these models reveal mutation fitness effects, epistasis, and the structural, functional, and evolutionary constraints encoded in protein sequences.

entry.title: Quantitative Biology 2026：Systems and Physical Biology
entry.content: July 22 – The Quantitative Biology 2026: Systems and Physical Biology Conference took place in Beijing from July 20 to 23, 2026. Homeostasis serves as a fundamental prerequisite for sustaining life and human health. Centered on the theme of “Systems and Physical Biology”, the conference aims to explore cutting-edge frontiers in quantitative biology and foster interdisciplinary exchanges among physicists, biologists, mathematicians and computer scientists. Its agenda covers state-of-the-art research across a broad spectrum of fields, including but not limited to: 1. Non-equilibrium dynamics and active biological matter 2. Multiscale biological networks 3. Design principles of living systems 4. Artificial intelligence and biological complexity. Dr. Huixia Ren presented a lecture entitled Global Synchronization of Pancreatic Islets Maintains Fasting Glycemia In Vivo.

entry.content: On July 19, 2026, Professor Kim Sneppen, Member of the Royal Danish Academy of Sciences and Letters, visited the laboratory for academic exchange. Professor Sneppen discussed ongoing research projects with Yawen Deng, Sen Yang, Xuejiao Wang, Dan Li and Chunmei Zhou, and shared mathematical model of islet synchronization. In the evening, the group headed to the China World Hotel to enjoy the city skyline.

entry.title: PhD Qualifying Examination by Yawen Deng, PhD Candidate

link.title: PhD Qualifying Examination by Yawen Deng, PhD Candidate

entry.content: PhD candidate Yawen Deng recently completed her PhD Qualifying Examination with a presentation titled “Role of α–β Cell Interaction in Regulating In Vivo Islet Ca²⁺ Dynamics and Glucose Homeostasis.” Her research focuses on how communication between pancreatic α and β cells helps coordinate islet activity and maintain stable blood glucose levels. By studying islet Ca²⁺ dynamics in vivo, the project aims to better understand how intra-islet interactions are organized under physiological and diabetic conditions. Preliminary findings suggest that blood glucose levels influence islet Ca²⁺ rhythmicity, and that disrupted α–β cell communication may contribute to impaired insulin secretion and unstable glucose homeostasis in metabolic disease. This defense session marked a key milestone in her doctoral research journeys, with her proposed studies promising to provide a framework for using in vivo islet Ca²⁺ rhythms as a dynamic indicator of islet cell communication and may offer new insight into the mechanisms underlying diabetes-related islet dysfunction. Congratulations!
